name: Rainbow Countdown Sticker
tagline: The app's own rainbow timer, die-cut like one of its stickers, with the time already spent cut clean out of it.
concept: This is the timer teachers watch all lesson, printed as one of the board's own stickers. A cream face sits inside a thick rainbow band, wrapped in a constant-width white die-cut on the amber canvas plate, and the time already spent is cut away as a deep, square-shouldered 110° notch at upper left that goes right down to the face edge. The outline stays closed because the timer's empty track, a thin warm-grey lane just inside the face, runs across the notch and tucks under both band ends. So the shape reads as a ring with time used up, not a C, spinner or refresh arrow, and that silhouette still identifies the app in macOS 26 tinted and clear modes, which strip colour. The band is one continuous OKLCH sweep taken from the red-to-magenta ring in timer.tsx, warmed and de-neoned into coral, tangerine, marigold, leaf, teal-sky and violet, with no hard joins, no Google primaries and no glow. The white die-cut stays at least 1px wide even at 16px so red and green never sit directly on amber for colour-blind viewers, and the plate has two flat facets, top-left light, warm grey-green shadows and a cream outline so it separates on the app's own amber canvas. Icon and glyph are one drawing. The glyph is exactly the colour icon's band plus track: the same 250° band, the same notch down to the face edge and the same tucked track ends. The dark icon re-lights that drawing with a deeper plate, a toned-down sticker and a dark face, and the small master redraws it flat on a 32-unit grid for 16–32px.
glyphNotes: The glyph is fitted to a 16px grid (64 units = 1px, major edges on multiples of 64): a 3px band (r 320–512) with the spent 110° cut a full 3px deep, closed by a solid 2px track (r 192–320) whose ends curl up into the band. The counter is at least 6px (7.6px inscribed) and nothing is thinner than 2px. At 18px it reads as a ring with a clean square bite out of its upper left, an outline no clock, record, spinner or refresh symbol has. While a timer runs, the band starts as a full ring, its trailing end steps back anticlockwise towards 12 o'clock and the notch widens. At time's up only the thin track ring is left; it blinks against the full ring three times, then stays until clicked.
direction: Countdown Sticker — the panel winner, final

name: Nibbled Countdown
tagline: The app's rainbow timer as one of its own die-cut stickers, with its hamster standing in the bite where the spent time has been nibbled away.
concept:
The panel's winning sticker and its favourite character become one object. It is Classroom Widgets' rainbow countdown ring, die-cut like the app's own stickers, with the spent time cut away as a squared bite of about 115° at upper-left. The timer's real hamster (its exact creatures.tsx markup, about a third of the ring's width) stands on the empty track inside that bite, facing the violet leading cap as if it has just nibbled the missing minutes. Its white die-cut joins the sticker's outline, so the character breaks the silhouette and still identifies the app in macOS 26 tinted and clear modes, which strip the colour.

The ring is a warm continuous sweep derived from the gradient in timer.tsx: coral → tangerine → marigold → leaf → teal/sky → violet, blended in OKLCH with no hard joins, no neon, no Google primaries and no halo. The band is slimmer than round 3's donut and sits on the amber-canvas plate, which has two flat facets, one top-left light and a cream outline so it separates on the board. The bite shows the app's warm-gray-200 track instead of mint. A constant-width white rim, kept at every size down to the 16px favicon, separates the colours for colour-blind users. The dark appearance re-lights it as the widget's own dark mode: deep amber plate, toned-down cream sticker, warm-gray-800 face and warm-gray-700 track, with no glare.

The glyph is the same drawing in one tone on the 16px grid. It keeps the same wedge and puts the hamster at the same spot and angle, redrawn as a purpose-built side profile. The small master flattens the same composition: fat band, 64-unit rim, and a flat version of the app's hamster with its two dot eyes at 32px. At 16–24px the small master shows the ring alone, because the hamster smudges into the bite there; an @media (max-width:24px) rule inside the one file switches it off.

Live in the menu bar, the band retreats counter-clockwise from its leading cut in axis-snapped frames, so the cuts at 6 and 3 o'clock stay pixel-crisp. The spent part is drawn as the 2px closing track, so the outline never opens, and the hamster stays in its bite. At time's up only that thin closed track remains, an empty wheel with its hamster on top, and it blinks twice like the widget's Time's Up.
glyphNotes: At 18px and at true 16px it reads as a bold timer ring with a squared bite at upper-left and a small critter sitting in it (head bump, dip, curled-tail bump), 2.2–3.5px clear of both ring ends. At 18pt@2x the side profile is plainly the hamster: big round head, snout, one 2px ear, stubby feet fused into the base and a curly tail, with no eyes, so it reads as neither Mickey nor a skull. The silhouette is one closed #000 even-odd path on the 64-unit grid: ring centre (576,576), band 192 units / 3px (r256–448), closing track 128 units / 2px (r192–320), crisp vertical and horizontal cuts at x704 and y640, and no feature under 64 units (ear 128, tail 102). The outer notch step is 2px plus a 1px inner lip, not the requested 3px, to keep the counter round at 7–8px.

direction: The hamster ate the spent time

name: Hamster at Home
tagline: The app's own hamster, sitting on the face of the rainbow countdown sticker whose spent time is cut away.
concept: It is the timer every class watches, told with its own creature: the app's exact calm hamster (the creatures.tsx markup under one mirrored transform, 10% smaller than round 3, facing right as it does when it runs along the bottom of the real ring) sits large on the cream face of a die-cut rainbow sticker, and the spent ~110° is cut out of the sticker at the upper-left, with squared, softened shoulders at 12 and 8 o'clock, a pale warm-grey track closing the gap and the white rim drawn as one constant 25-unit offset with no pinch. The ring is a warm continuous sweep taken from timer.tsx's red-to-magenta gradient but de-neoned (coral, tangerine, marigold, leaf, sea-green, sky, violet, blended in OKLab with no hard joins) on the amber canvas plate with two facets, one top-left light, soft olive-brown shadows and no cream halo; the dark appearance deepens the plate, tones the rim down, turns the face to the widget's warm charcoal and gives the hamster a thin tan die-cut edge so it still clears 3:1. The small master keeps the same sticker, sweep and notch on a 32-unit grid with a flat hamster (2px eyes and tail at 32px, heavier outline, no feet or glints), and the menu-bar glyph is that notched sticker as solid ink, like a rubber stamp of it, with a purpose-built side-profile hamster knocked out of the face, so all three stay one mark even in macOS tinted and clear modes, where only the silhouette survives. Live, the hamster hops out while a timer runs (it is off running the ring), and the stamp's bite sweeps counter-clockwise from 8 o'clock in whole-pixel steps until only the round core is left; at zero the core blinks twice, like the widget's Time's Up, and the hamster comes home.
glyphNotes: At 16px it is a solid 14px disc (R = 7px) with a clean 2px bite out of its upper-left, a vertical step at 12 o'clock and a horizontal one at 8, and an 8x5px hamster-shaped window with at least 2px of ink around it (about 42% ink, 20% grey pixels), which from 18px and at 18pt @2x resolves into the side profile: round head at the front, one ear, fused feet and the curly tail. The silhouette is the colour sticker's die-cut outline, its bite deepened to a whole 2px, filled solid with the hamster knocked out of the face, so it cannot become a C, a spinner, a refresh arrow, a Mickey head or a skull.

name: Gold Star Timer
tagline: The app's own gold star sticker, slapped over the rim of its rainbow countdown: the timer and the reward in one mark.
concept: This is Classroom Widgets' real timer: a cream face and the widget's own horizontal rainbow gradient (red at 9, green at 12 and 6, violet at 3) with its round caps, drained by a quarter so only the thin pale track remains from 9 to 12, which is how the widget actually depletes. On top sits the app's Font Awesome star sticker (orange-500 with a lighter centre, thick white die-cut border, down-right shadow, tilted +15° in the app's 5° steps), slapped big over the rim at 4:40 as a co-hero rather than a badge, and ring, rim and star all sit inside the 80% maskable circle. It is exactly what a class sees on the board, the countdown plus the gold star at time's up. The amber plate is the app's canvas, with a thin cream edge so it separates when shown on that canvas, and the face is left empty; the dark variant uses the app's dark-mode timer (warm-grey face, toned rainbow) and keeps a toned warm-white border so the orange star never sinks into the deep caramel plate. With no numeral, identity comes from the ring itself: its outer edge is a clean closed circle, the spent quarter is a thinner track rather than a gap, and its only opening is where the star physically covers it, bounded by star-shaped occlusion edges, so it cannot read as a C, a spinner or a refresh arrow. The glyph is the icon with colour removed: the same geometry refit to the box at SF Symbols weight, with the star's white die-cut border becoming a 104-unit knockout; in the live menu-bar state the thick band retreats from its 9 o'clock cap back toward 12 over the track as a timer runs, the star stays stuck at 4:40, and at zero only the track and the star remain while the star gives one bounce.
glyphNotes: At 18px it reads as a closed timer ring (2.2px band, with a 1.5px thinner quarter at upper left for the spent time) broken only at lower right by a chunky 7.6px five-point star across a 1.8px die-cut gap. That makes it a sticker on a ring rather than a C, G, magnifier or refresh arrow, since there is no arrowhead and no round-capped opening. The silhouette is one solid ring piece plus one solid Font Awesome star in #000 only; the smallest features are the 66-unit star tips, the 84-unit track and the 104-unit moat.

name: Mini Board
tagline: The projected board in one glance: the rainbow timer out front, the name-picker card tucked behind it, and an orange star sticker pinning the two together.
concept: A thumbnail of the board teachers actually project. It keeps the client's round-2 charm but is rebuilt to hold at every size. The hero is the app's cream timer face (left empty) in its round-capped rainbow ring. Tucked behind it is the randomiser card with its real purple→pink→amber reel: faded names peek in at top and bottom, and the chosen name sits bold on a white chip. The app's own Font Awesome star sticker, in orange with a thick white die-cut border, pins the card's corner where it meets the timer's rim, and a few flecks of the red/yellow/teal/navy confetti finish the scene. Everything sits inside the 80% maskable circle on the amber canvas plate, which has two large facets and a cream keyline so it separates on the app's own canvas. With no numeral, the ring gets its identity from its spent sixth and from what surrounds it. From 10 to 12 o'clock the rainbow steps down onto a thin track, so every rendering is a closed, notched O with round caps, never a C, spinner or refresh arrow, while the card behind it and the star in its crook make it the board. The star sits outside the ring, never in a gap, so nothing reads as a crescent-and-star, cloud or sync badge. Each size gets its own rendering: the full scene from 64 px up; a macOS dark variant re-lit with a walnut plate, warm-grey card frame, the app's dark timer face with a dark spent channel, toned rims and no glare; a flat small master for 16–32 px that keeps only card, ring and star, bigger, with two white name bars, a smooth sweep, white die-cut borders, no confetti or facets, snapped to the grid; and a one-tone glyph that is the same drawing with colour removed, where the white rims become 64-unit knockouts. Live menu-bar state: while a timer runs, the glyph's thick band retreats counter-clockwise onto the thin track in step with the in-app ring, and at zero only the track, the card and the star remain.
glyphNotes: At 18 pt it reads as an outlined name card (a frame plus two name bars) with a bold, closed timer ring overlapping its lower-right and a solid star pinning its lower-left corner. It is one #000 path drawn on the 16 px grid (1 px frame and name bars, 2 px ring, 5–6 px star, 1 px knockouts), so it stays crisp at true 1x in the Windows tray and GNOME bar and sits at SF Symbols weight beside Wi-Fi and Control Centre; the ring is the heaviest stroke, and its 60° spent notch, the same notch the colour icon draws as its pale track, shows from 18 pt @2x up.
